gap: The IBM CSV has blank TotalCharges values for new customers, but the paper does not state how to coerce or impute them before min-max scaling.
options: coerce to numeric and impute 0 when tenure is 0
chosen: coerce TotalCharges to numeric and impute blank/NaN as 0 before scaling
rationale: Blank TotalCharges correspond to new customers with tenure 0, so 0 preserves the known billing relationship and retains all 7,043 records.

gap: No random seed is stated for the stratified split, SMOTE, Random Forest, or cross-validation.
rationale: A fixed seed is needed for deterministic reproduction; the paper reports only point estimates and fold means.

gap: The paper states min-max scaling but not whether the scaler is fit before or after the train-test split.
options: fit on the training partition only and transform test
fit on the full dataset before splitting
chosen: split first, fit MinMaxScaler on the training partition only, and transform the test partition
rationale: Avoids test-set leakage and follows standard leakage-safe reproduction practice, though min-max ranges may differ slightly from the paper.
quote: Continuous features are min-max scaled to [0,1]. A stratified 80/20 train–test split preserves the class ratio

gap: The paper does not specify whether SMOTE is applied before or after min-max scaling.
options: scale training data, then apply SMOTE
scale the full dataset, split, then apply SMOTE to training
chosen: split, fit scaler on training, transform train/test, then apply SMOTE to the training partition only
rationale: Prevents synthetic points from influencing the scaler and keeps all test data untouched.
quote: SMOTE is applied exclusively to training data: synthetic minority instances are interpolated

gap: Only L2 regularisation is stated for Logistic Regression; solver, C, max_iter, and class_weight are unspecified.
chosen: scikit-learn LogisticRegression(penalty='l2', C=1.0, solver='lbfgs', max_iter=1000, class_weight=None)
rationale: Standard default L2 baseline; class_weight is unnecessary because SMOTE already balances the training partition.
quote: Logistic Regression (l2 regularisation) serves as the interpretable linear baseline

gap: The paper does not state whether one-hot encoding drops a reference level.
options: drop the first level per categorical feature
rationale: Only keeping all levels yields the paper's stated 40-dimensional feature space and matches LinearExplainer's use of the design matrix.

gap: The mapping of yes/no and gender categories to 0/1 is not specified.
chosen: Yes=1 and No=0; Male=1 and Female=0; use SeniorCitizen as provided
rationale: Binary recoding flips coefficient signs but not predicted probabilities or AUC, so impact on C1 is low.
quote: Gender and binary yes/no features (Partner, Dependents, PhoneService, PaperlessBilling) are label-encoded to {0,1}.

gap: The paper reports precision, recall, and F1 but does not explicitly define which class is positive.
chosen: churn=1 is positive for precision, recall, F1, and AUC
rationale: Matches the churn-risk use case and the reported LR recall of 78.34%, which targets churners.
quote: The binary outcome variable indicates whether each customer churned

gap: No XGBoost or LightGBM hyperparameters are reported beyond using the official libraries.
chosen: official library defaults with random_state=42 and the 0.5 threshold, no tuning
rationale: The paper gives no search procedure; defaults are the only reproducible choice, but exact 78.42% and 0.8306 may not reproduce.
quote: the pipeline uses the official XGBoost and LightGBM libraries directly

gap: The paper reports 5-fold stratified cross-validation with scaling and SMOTE refit inside each fold but not the fold seed or whether models share folds.
chosen: shared shuffled stratified 5-fold with seed 42; refit scaler and SMOTE inside each training fold
rationale: The paper explicitly refits inside each fold to avoid leakage; shared folds make model comparisons paired.
quote: we ran 5-fold stratified cross-validation with feature scaling and SMOTE refit inside each fold to preclude leakage

gap: The paper warns that SMOTE-trained probabilities are inflated relative to deployment prevalence but does not apply recalibration to the reported results.
options: use raw SMOTE-trained probabilities for metrics and tiering
chosen: use raw probabilities for reported AUC and tier distribution; do not recalibrate
rationale: Matches the reported 0.8411 and tier percentages; calibration is presented only as a production recommendation.
quote: its output probabilities are inflated relative to the 26.5% deployment prevalence

gap: The top-20% business-impact precision and recall appear to be computed on the full 7,043 cohort, not explicitly on the 1,409 held-out test set.
options: recompute on the held-out test set only
chosen: treat the 937/1,408 calculation as an illustrative full-cohort projection, not a held-out test metric
rationale: The paper says full cohort of 7,043 and calls the business figures illustrative, so this should not be targeted as a reproduction metric.
quote: Targeting the top 20% of the subscriber base by predicted churn probability (approximately 1,408 customers from the full cohort of 7,043)
